title: Pseudonym derivation pipeline is fully built and never wired up
description:
Three public APIs form a complete per-consumer pseudonym pipeline, each with tests, and no caller anywhere in the workspace:

- persona-core/src/pseudonym.rs:13 `derive_pseudonym(ikm, trust_domain, consumer_app_id)` — 7 tests, three with proper pyca/cryptography HKDF oracles
- persona-core/src/consumer.rs:47 `ConsumerIdentity::selector_key()` — documented as "a stable string key suitable for use as HKDF `info`", i.e. the second argument to the above; 7 tests
- persona-core/src/spiffe_id.rs:106 `SpiffeId::pseudonymous(trust_domain, hkdf_id, consumer)` — builds the resulting `pseudonym/{hkdf_id}/for/{consumer}` ID

Grep confirms the only references are the definitions, the `pub use` in persona-core/src/lib.rs:14-16, and their own tests. persona-grpc/src/service.rs issues SVIDs with `claim.spiffe_id.uri()` directly (line 175) — the real, non-pseudonymous ID — so no consumer ever receives a blinded identity.

The gap is structural, not a missing call: the pipeline needs a `ConsumerIdentity` to derive against, and that comes from `consumer_attest::attest_peer`, which is itself never called (filed separately). Both halves are complete and neither is connected.

This is worth an issue rather than deletion — the code is correct and tested, and per-consumer blinding is clearly an intended feature. But right now the crate exports a privacy feature that does nothing, and the tests give false confidence that it is in use.

Fix: either wire it up behind the peer attestation work, or add a note on `derive_pseudonym` stating it is not yet on the issuance path and naming the issue that will connect it.
close_reason: Duplicate of persona-5s4b.41 (same defect, filed by a second review agent from a different angle). Merged during review triage; reopen if the angle in this issue is not covered there.
